+# Gate 12 Baseline
+
+Gate 12 began from merged `main` commit `a2a1eace`. The matched matrix used
+the pinned x86-64 sysbench binary, Q35 under TCG, 2 GiB memory, nine samples
+per workload cell, and identical vCPU/thread topology for Rocky-on-Linux and
+Rocky-on-Ginux.
+
+The table reports the favorable-direction Ginux/Linux ratio. Values below the
+gate floor of `0.96x` are marked **fail**.
+
+| Mode | vCPUs | Threads | CPU | Memory | Thread yield | Mutex |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| fixed | 1 | 1 | 1.216x | 1.169x | 0.994x | 1.079x |
+| fixed | 2 | 1 | 1.075x | 1.140x | **0.346x fail** | 1.079x |
+| fixed | 4 | 1 | 1.039x | 1.096x | **0.323x fail** | 1.050x |
+| scaled | 2 | 2 | 1.228x | 1.044x | 1.123x | **0.810x fail** |
+| scaled | 4 | 4 | **0.595x fail** | **0.668x fail** | **0.014x fail** | **0.389x fail** |
+
+The fixed 2-vCPU thread-yield profile recorded about 1.27 million syscalls per
+four-second sample: roughly half `futex` and half `sched_yield`. The main CPU
+returned a successful spurious futex wake while the single remote worker ran,
+causing userspace to re-enter the kernel continuously. The 4-vCPU result also
+matches the implementation limit of one remote runtime-thread job pinned to
+CPU 1; CPUs 2 and 3 cannot execute Linux runtime threads.
+
+Raw generated results remain under `build/benchmark/gate12-baseline/` in the
+working tree and are intentionally not committed.

+# Gate 12 Performance Parity
+
+Gate 12 compared the same pinned x86-64 sysbench binary on Rocky Linux under
+Linux and Rocky Linux userspace under Ginux. Both sides used Q35 under QEMU
+TCG, 2 GiB memory, identical one-, two-, and four-vCPU topologies, and nine
+samples per workload cell. Ratios below use the favorable direction: higher
+throughput is better for CPU, memory, and thread yield; lower elapsed time is
+better for mutex.
+
+## Result
+
+Every cell meets the approved `0.96x` floor. Eighteen of the twenty unique
+cells beat Linux. Fixed 2-vCPU CPU throughput reached `0.982x`, and scaled
+4-vCPU mutex reached `0.970x`; both are within the accepted two-to-four-percent
+band but did not reach the stronger faster-than-Linux target.
+
+| Mode | vCPUs | Threads | CPU | Memory | Thread yield | Mutex |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| fixed | 1 | 1 | 2.185x | 2.342x | 1.312x | 2.163x |
+| fixed | 2 | 1 | 0.982x | 1.122x | 2.995x | 1.066x |
+| fixed | 4 | 1 | 1.002x | 1.101x | 2.912x | 1.036x |
+| scaled | 2 | 2 | 1.186x | 1.207x | 4.090x | 1.070x |
+| scaled | 4 | 4 | 1.173x | 1.138x | 2.583x | 0.970x |
+
+## Before and after
+
+The merged Gate 11 baseline had seven failing cells. The largest gaps were
+scaled 4-vCPU thread yield at `0.014x`, mutex at `0.389x`, CPU at `0.595x`,
+and memory at `0.668x`. Gate 12 changed general runtime mechanisms rather than
+recognizing or special-casing sysbench:
+
+- a remote `sched_yield` fast path stopped needlessly serializing a thread
+  that could only select itself;
+- Linux runtime jobs and ownership publication became per-CPU, allowing all
+  online application CPUs to execute independent Linux threads;
+- futex wait publication and wakeup gained a coordinated boundary;
+- safe fast syscalls remain available while an interval timer is armed but no
+  signal is pending; and
+- Linux `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` and `FUTEX_WAKE_BITSET` masks, absolute timeout
+  semantics, and sixth-argument wiring were implemented. A guarded remote-
+  worker path removed a userspace retry storm caused by rejecting valid glibc
+  futex operations.
+
+Profiling found roughly 699,000 operation-265 observations in one pre-fix
+scaled memory sample. Operation 265 is
+`FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET|FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME`; Ginux had returned `EINVAL`, causing
+glibc to re-enter the kernel continuously. After correction, focused scaled
+memory and mutex medians crossed the acceptance floor, and the final complete
+matrix confirmed the result.
+
+## Qualification
+
+The final code passed:
+
+- `make check`
+- `make architecture-check`
+- `make test-smp`
+- `make test-rocky-smp-futex`
+- `make test-rocky-smp-shared-page`
+- `make test-rocky-smp-thread-context`
+
+The final matrix contains nine Linux and nine Ginux samples in every sysbench
+cell and uses the same binary digest throughout. Boot measurements remain
+observational because Linux and Ginux follow different startup paths. These
+results characterize this QEMU TCG experiment; they are not native-hardware or
+general production-performance claims.

+# Gate 12: UP and SMP Performance Parity
+
+## Goal
+
+Make Rocky-on-Ginux meet or beat matched Rocky-on-Linux performance across the
+complete fixed-thread and scaled-thread benchmark matrix. A result within four
+percent of Linux is acceptable; the target is faster than Linux in every cell.
+
+## Approved scope
+
+- Reproduce and freeze fresh merged-`main` Linux and Ginux baselines.
+- Profile scheduler, yield, futex, context-switch, timer, IPI, memory, and
+  related kernel paths with bounded diagnostics that are disabled by default.
+- Optimize general kernel mechanisms in order of measured impact.
+- Run targeted benchmark cells during iteration and the complete matrix for
+  final acceptance.
+- Add deterministic correctness or performance regressions for mechanisms
+  changed by the gate.
+- Publish before/after results, profiling evidence, implementation rationale,
+  and remaining limitations.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- Sysbench-specific kernel behavior, benchmark detection, or workload changes.
+- Different QEMU resources, binaries, sample counts, or durations for Linux and
+  Ginux.
+- Native-hardware or broad production-performance claims.
+- Treating boot timing as a kernel-speed comparison or a passage criterion.
+- Unrelated feature, compatibility, UI, storage, or networking work.
+- Weakening correctness, security, isolation, or prior gate acceptance.
+
+## Completed work
+
+- [x] Confirm PR #7 merged cleanly into `main`.
+- [x] Create `codex/performance-parity` from merged `main`.
+- [x] Align the goal, scope, acceptance threshold, review policy, and delivery
+  strategy with the human.
+- [x] Reproduce and preserve a fresh complete baseline.
+- [x] Add bounded child-exit profiling and attribute the first dominant costs.
+- [x] Generalize remote Linux runtime-thread dispatch across every online
+  application CPU.
+- [x] Add coordinated futex wait/wake fast paths and preserve prior SMP
+  correctness regressions.
+- [x] Implement Linux futex bitset masks and absolute timeout semantics, and
+  remove the glibc bitset-wait retry storm.
+
+## Remaining work
+
+- [x] Optimize measured general kernel mechanisms.
+- [x] Add regression coverage for changed mechanisms.
+- [x] Re-run targeted cells until stable.
+- [x] Run and validate the complete matched matrix.
+- [x] Publish final evidence and stop for human review.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- Fixed-mode workloads use one thread at one, two, and four vCPUs.
+- Scaled-mode workloads use one, two, and four threads at the corresponding
